what_it_does: AQB8 is a specialized hardware chip for speeding up ray tracing—a rendering technique that simulates light bouncing off objects to create photorealistic images. Modern ray tracers use a data structure called a Bounding Volume Hierarchy (BVH), essentially a tree of boxes that tell the ray where objects are. Currently, these boxes are stored as 32-bit floating-point numbers (precise but memory-heavy), which slows rendering by consuming huge amounts of memory bandwidth. AQB8 uses an insight: you can represent bounding boxes as 8-bit integers (much more compact) while still calculating ray-box intersections correctly. The hardware replaces expensive 32-bit math units with simple integer arithmetic and adds error-compensation across the tree to ensure no rays incorrectly pass through boxes.
